title: Dionysus: the god of wine and excess
subtitle: Wine, theater, transgression
subject: mythologie
description: God of wine and ecstasy, Dionysus is also the patron of Greek theater. Born twice, he abolishes the boundaries between order and chaos.

hero.hook: The god of wine not only brings intoxication: he also invents theater.

blocks.text: **Dionysus** is the most paradoxical Greek god. God of wine, the vine and intoxication, he is above all the god of metamorphosis. Unlike the Olympians frozen on their summit, he wanders, followed by a noisy procession.
It abolishes the boundaries between divine and human, order and chaos, life and death. From its festivals will be born the [[Theatre]], one of the greatest legacies of Greece.

sections.title: Born twice: from Semele to the thigh of Zeus

blocks.text: Dionysus is born from a tragedy. **Zeus**, king of the gods, loves the mortal , princess of Thebes. **Hera**, Zeus's jealous wife, pushes her to demand that her lover show himself in his true divine form. [[Semele]]

blocks.caption: Dionysus, god of wine, ecstasy and metamorphosis.

blocks.text: Zeus complies. Lightning kills Semele. To save the child, Zeus places him in his own thigh until birth. Dionysus was therefore “twice born”, hence the song dedicated to him: . [[Dithyramb]]
This myth explains why Dionysus is both mortal and divine: he has a human mother and an Olympian father who “carried” him.

As an adult, Dionysus travels the world to spread his cult. His followers, especially women called **Maenades** or Bacchantes, leave the city for the mountains. There, dance, music and wine provoke a trance: being “possessed by the god”.
These rites, called , overturn the social order. For one night, reason gives way. The god promises liberation, but also madness for those who refuse it. [[Mysteries]]

blocks.caption: Bacchantes in trance: the cult which overthrows the order of the city.

blocks.text: One day, pirates capture Dionysus to sell him. He changes the oars into snakes and makes vines grow on the mast. Terrified, the men jump into the sea and become dolphins.

In Athens, this god of excess becomes the patron of a civic art: the theater. In the 6th century BC, the **Great Dionysia** organized dramatic competitions. Everything starts from the dithyramb, a choral song in honor of the god.

blocks.caption: The Great Dionysia: worship becomes a city spectacle.

blocks.text: When a singer breaks away from the chorus to respond, the actor is born. Tragedy becomes a place where the city looks at its fears and conflicts without sinking into real chaos. It's : purging yourself of emotions by looking at them. [[Catharsis]]

events.title: Double birth
events.detail: Semele dies; Zeus completes the gestation.

blocks.text: In the 19th century, the philosopher **Nietzsche** opposed two forces: , god of measurement and clarity, and Dionysus, force of intoxication and creative chaos. This tension, the [[Apollo]], explains for him the greatness of Greek tragedy. [[Apollonian and Dionysian (Nietzsche)]]
Dionysus thus remains the god who recalls a simple truth: without a little disorder, there is no art, no celebration, no invention.
**Dionysus**, twice born, god of wine and ecstasy, inspires the rites that give birth to the Greek **theater**. He embodies the fruitful tension between moderation and excess.
